verdicts.note: A levy lid lift, which pole_b names as a cap lift, raising the rate from $0.228924 to $0.35 per $1,000, about 53% (S1, S2, S3). The 'restore' framing does not make it a renewal. Strength 2 matches Lewis's and Thurston's mapping of the same measure. No spending mapping: the stated purpose is maintaining and restoring service cut in 2026 (S1, S2).

Attacked toward 2, because the dollar amounts rise each year, from $994,006 to $1,217,701 (S1, S2). But it replaces an expiring 2022 levy at the same maximum rate, $1.97 per $1,000 (S3), so the renewal tier (+1) applies. That is consistent with Lewis's Chehalis TBD and the Spokane and Benton replacement school levies. No parental-rights mapping: it is an operations levy, and the dossier has nothing on curricula, notification or opt-outs.

New general obligation bonds ($12.8 million), repaid by a new excess property tax estimated at $1.42 per $1,000 for up to 21 years (S1, S3). The dossier calls it a new bond, not a replacement (S3). +2 is supported. No parental-rights mapping: capital improvements only.

Attacked from both sides. Toward 2: the levy amounts rise from $3.7 million to $4.04 million. Toward omission: there is no current-rate comparison, so the size of any change is unknown. Neither holds. It replaces a levy that otherwise ends after 2027 (S1, S2), and the renewal tier (+1) is the conservative reading the dossier supports. S1 and S2 support it. No parental-rights mapping.

Raises the TBD sales tax from 0.2% to 0.3% for ten years (S1, S2). It is an increase on top of the 0.2% renewed in 2025 (S3, S4), not a renewal, so +2 is supported. No local-control mapping: the city is voting on its own TBD tax, and the dossier records no state-versus-local dispute.

what_it_does matches the ballot title and explanatory statement (S1, S2): $0.22 to $0.35 for 2027 and 2028, the 2028 amount as the base, restoring hours, staffing and collections. The Shelton, Belfair and Hoodsport branches come from the Mason statement for (S1), and the five-county vote from S2. cost_line matches S1/S2 ($0.228924; $40.44 on $334,000) and S3 (TRL's $43 on the $333,773 Mason median). pro_summary paraphrases the TimberStrong Libraries Committee's Mason statement (S1) accurately, including the Hoodsport staffing warning. con_summary attributes the statement against to Citizens for Accountable TR Libraries (Sean Swope) as S1 prints it. Its closing quote drops the quotation marks around 'No' in 'Voting "No" is not a vote against libraries or literacy', a cosmetic difference.

what_it_does and cost_line match S1/S2 (four years, 2027-2030; $994,006 to $1,217,701; $1.97 per $1,000 each year; the listed uses) and S3 (the same maximum rate approved in 2022). pro_summary quotes the Huffs' statement for accurately (S1). con_summary matches S1 (no statement against) and S4 (no committee).

what_it_does matches the ballot title (S1, S2): $12.8 million, 21 years, the listed security and facility work. The note that only the Mason portion of the district votes here is a scoping fact, not a dossier claim. cost_line's $1.42 per $1,000 and $426 on $300,000 come from the district (S3). pro_summary correctly says no statement for was filed (S1) and draws the district's purpose and the failed February 2026 bond from S3. con_summary matches S1 and S5.

what_it_does and cost_line match S1/S2: it replaces a levy expiring after 2027, runs 2028-2031, collects $3,700,000 to $4,043,090 at $1.18 to $1.15 per $1,000, and has the listed uses. pro_summary and con_summary match S1/S2 (neither statement filed) and S4 (no committee).

what_it_does and cost_line match S1/S2: 0.2% to 0.3% for ten years, the listed uses, paid by anyone buying in the city, no revenue estimate. pro_summary: no statement for was filed (S1, S2). The council's July 2026 unanimous vote was a preliminary approval, with a final vote set for July 21 (S3). 'Voted unanimously ... to move the increase toward the ballot' describes that preliminary step accurately. con_summary matches S1/S2 and S5.
